name: Scale AI
summary: Scale AI provides data, evaluation, and safety infrastructure used to build and assess artificial-intelligence systems.
overview: Scale AI supplies data operations and evaluation infrastructure for AI developers, enterprises, and public-sector customers.

facts.label: Latest valuation context
facts.note: Meta's June 2025 investment valued Scale at $29B.

bull_case: Evaluation and high-quality data remain essential as models become more capable and more widely deployed.
bear_case: Customer concentration and the shift in leadership after Meta's investment could complicate the independent business.
directory_notes: Meta acquired a 49% non-voting stake, per reported transaction terms.
Evaluation, enterprise AI, and public-sector demand.

intelligence.description: Scale AI supplies the data, evaluation, and safety layer behind AI systems. Its test is whether model builders and enterprises will keep outsourcing high-stakes data work as internal capabilities expand.
company: Scale AI began as a provider of labeled training data and developed into a broader AI infrastructure company offering data, model evaluation, safety, and agent-focused services. It works across commercial and government applications where model reliability is a production constraint.

Meta's June 2025 investment and the move of Scale co-founder Alexandr Wang to Meta reshaped the company. Scale remains a private business, but the transaction made independence, customer relationships, and governance central questions for its next phase.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Scale sits at a bottleneck in the AI economy: trustworthy training data and evaluation. Its trajectory is a read-through on whether value accrues to model companies, infrastructure vendors, or the operational layer that makes models usable in the real world.

changed.text: Scale's data-labeling business became a major supplier to autonomous-vehicle and AI developers.
Raised capital at a $13.8B valuation as generative-AI evaluation demand accelerated.
Meta invested a reported $14.3B for a 49% non-voting stake, valuing Scale at $29B.

takeaways: Scale is most valuable where data quality, evaluation, and human-in-the-loop operations remain difficult to automate.
Meta's investment validates its strategic importance but also creates customer-perception and governance questions.
The opportunity expands with enterprise AI deployment, where reliability matters as much as model capability.
Concentration among a few large model developers and competitive in-house tooling remain key risks.
